transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I've been having some trouble at work lately. It's just... during our long sales strategy meetings, I keep getting up. I know I'm supposed to stay seated, but I just end up getting up anyway, even if it's just to refill my water or pace by the printer.
Do you also find yourself getting up frequently or feeling restless in other situations, like at home or in social settings?
I guess... maybe a little? I don't really know. I just... I like to keep moving, I suppose. It's not a big deal.
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to stay seated even when you're not at work, like when you're watching TV or sitting in a meeting at home?

I mean... I don't really pay attention to that. If I'm watching a show, I might get up to do something, but... I haven't really noticed it being hard to just sit on my couch. Like I said, it's mostly just... at the office.
How do you feel when you're in situations that aren't work-related, like sitting in a restaurant or waiting room? Do you find it hard to stay seated then, or feel unusually restless?

Um... I don't know. I guess waiting rooms are just boring for anyone, right? I might shift around a bit or check my phone, but... I don't think I feel unusually restless. It's just normal waiting. And restaurants are fine. I just sit and eat. I haven't really thought about it.

Outside of work and the places you just mentioned, do you ever notice yourself feeling restless or needing to get up and move around during other everyday activities, like sitting at a friend's house or waiting for something?
Not really. I mean... no, I don't think so. If I'm at a friend's house, we're usually talking or doing something, so... it's fine. I just don't really notice anything like that.
Can you think of a time when you weren't at work or in a meeting where you felt the need to get up or move around even though you knew you should stay seated?
I... no. I really can't think of anything. Like I said, it's mostly just a work thing. I don't really have that issue other places.
As we're sitting here talking, do you feel any urge to get up or move around, or are you comfortable staying seated?
No... I'm fine. I'm just sitting here.
Have you ever felt restless or needed to get up and move around during long car rides or while sitting alone reading or doing quiet work?
Um... no. I don't really read that much, to be honest. And car rides are... just car rides. I drive, or I sit there. I don't really think about it.
Do you ever find it hard to focus or get easily distracted during tasks or activities that aren't work-related, like reading, watching TV, or having a conversation?

Um... not really with TV or conversations, no. But... I guess if I'm reading something for work, like a client brief or sitting in a long strategy meeting... I can lose track. Like, I'll start out paying attention, but then after a few minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the same paragraph or slide for a while. I won't really know what was just said or what I just read. But... yeah, that's mostly just a work thing, too.
Outside of work, do you ever find it hard to focus or get distracted during activities like reading for pleasure, watching TV, or listening to a friend talk?
Um... no, not really. Like I said, TV and talking to friends are fine. I don't read much for fun anyway, so... it's just not an issue outside of work.
Have you ever had trouble keeping your mind on what you're doing during personal conversations or activities that you enjoy, even if it wasn't work-related?
No, I don't think so. I mean, if it's something I enjoy, I'm usually fine. It's really just the work stuff.

Do you ever have trouble staying focused or find your mind wandering when you're doing something that requires concentration, like following directions, solving a problem, or even just remembering something someone just told you, even if it's not work-related?
Um... no, not really. I mean, if it's outside of work, I don't really have those issues. I can follow directions fine and... remember things okay. It's really just the work stuff like I said.
Have you ever found it hard to focus or felt restless during activities you really enjoy, like a hobby, spending time with family, or doing something you love?
No. Like I've been saying... if it's something I actually want to do, I'm fine. I don't really have a problem paying attention to my hobbies or my family.
Have you ever found yourself losing track of time or not remembering parts of an activity, even if it wasn't work-related, like watching a movie or having a conversation with someone?
No, not really. I mean, if I'm watching a movie, I watch the movie. I don't really lose time like that.

Have you ever noticed yourself feeling distracted, losing focus, or having difficulty staying engaged during activities that are not work-related, even if you thought you were paying attention at the time?
I don't think so. I mean, if I'm doing something outside of work, I'm usually pretty engaged. I haven't really noticed any issues with that.
Do you ever find it hard to stay focused or feel restless during quiet tasks that require you to sit still and concentrate, like filling out forms, doing paperwork, or working on a project at home?

Yeah, I guess so. At work... if I have to sit through a long strategy meeting or read a client brief, it happens. I'll start out paying attention, but then a few minutes go by, and I realize I'm just staring at the same slide or paragraph. I won't have any idea what was just said.
Do you ever find it hard to stay focused or feel restless during quiet tasks at home that require you to sit still and concentrate, like filling out forms or working on a project?
I don't really know. Um... I don't really do a lot of paperwork at home. I just try to relax when I'm not at work.

Have you ever noticed yourself having trouble focusing or feeling restless while doing quiet tasks at home, even if it's just occasionally, like when you're trying to fill out a form, read something for yourself, or work on a project that needs your attention?
I'm not really sure what else to say about that. Like I mentioned, I don't really do those kinds of things at home. I just try to unwind.
